newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end in black on fund book-closures.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end in black on fund book-closures.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended in positive territory after being in the red for most of the day, as local funds bought key blue chip stocks at the close of their half-year accounts, dealers and analysts said.
The key Composite Index gained 1.60 points, or 0.15 percent, to 1,078.90, after having dipped to 1,070.95 earlier. The Second Board index rose 0.18 points to 562.84.
"It looks as if it was window-dressing by some local funds for the close of their books," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house on the sharp rise over the last half-hour of trading.

Repco shed 4.00 ringgit to 124.50. The company said on Monday it would be the main supplier of timber for construction firm Chase Perdana. Analysts said Repco's share price fell due to the news having already been factored in before it was released.
"Investors are now asking themselves 'what is in store for Malaysia beyond 1998?'," said Irene Tan, head of research at Vickers Ballas.

Several infrastructure projects are due for completion in 1998 in time for Kuala Lumpur's hosting of the Commonwealth Games that year. Analysts have projected corporate earnings growth to slow down after that.
Volume was at 204 million shares. Losers pipped gainers 349 to 238 with 160 shares unchanged and 125 untraded.
